to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

209
Promotion of literature on art and
culture in Goa
*661. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any schemes are in force
for the promotion of literature on art and
culture in Goa;
(b) what are the essential features of
the schemes;
(c) the projects undertaken/
implemented under the schemes during the
last three years in the State; and
(d) the details of financial assistance
granted to the State during the last three
years, year-wise?
Moderation in growth of credit to
high risk sectors
*662. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the banks
have been asked to moderate growth of
credit to high risk sectors;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that  a number
of the Public Sector Banks have objected
to it; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Conversion of loans in to equity in
CPSEs
*663. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the amount of
outstanding loans to CPSEs converted into
equity as part of the revival plan
recommended by BRPSE during the last
two years;
(b) the details of the fresh equity
infusion into CPSEs as part of revival;
(c) what is the current worth of
Government's fresh equity investment and
converted equity during the last two years;
(d) the details of the comparative worth,
if the worth has gone down; and
(e) if not, how much dividend have
Government earned over the last two years
over such equity in the CPSEs?

Development of tourist centres in
Rajasthan

the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Central Government
have prepared any draft for development
of various tourist centres in Rajasthan;
(b) whether Government have any plan
to develop new tourist centres also
alongwith the development of old tourist
centres;

(d) the names of the districts in
Rajasthan for whose development
proposals have been submitted to the
Central Government from the State

centres Central Government have planned
to develop out of them and the target fixed

the details thereof?
Labour Law Compliance Report

AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to
 state:
(a) whether the Institute of Company
Secretaries of India under his Ministry is

Labour Law  Compliance Report being

(c) the proposed Labour Audit or the
Labour Law Compliance Report will cover
which Labour Acts?
Identification of unexplored tourist
spots
*666. DR. ABHISHEK MANU
SINGHVI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during 2006
the tourist arrival touched 4.43 million after
having stagnated around two million for
decades; and

identify more tourist spots which are
unexplored in States like Bihar (Buddhist
destinations), Himachal Pradesh

etc.), Uttarakhand (Pauri, Tehri,
Devprayag, Ranikhet), Punjab (Hindu
Temples and Sikh Gurudwaras) and
Haryana (Panipat, Kurukshetra, etc.) under
the umbrella of 'Incredible India' so that
target foreign budget groups may visit India
in large numbers?
Raising investment in petrochemical
sector

CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government approved the
National Policy on Petrochemicals which
outlines the broad contours to raise
investment in the sector so that India does
not miss the opportunity in the Asian
petrochemical boom;
(b) whether Government will introduce
necessary incentives to boost private

investment in petroleum, chemical and
petrochemical investment regions;
(c) whether ONGC worked out
investment of Rs. 18,000 crore for
exploration and production of oil and gas
in the current financial year 2007-08;
(d) what are the main projects that

(e) by when the implementation of these
projects would start?

Mullaperiyar dam in Kerala
*668. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of dams in the country
which are more than 100 years old;
(b) whether any study has been
conducted on the safety of these dams;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government have received
any proposal to construct a new dam in
place of Mullaperiyar dam in Kerala, which
is older than 100 years; and
(e) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto and action taken in this regard?
Allocation of funds under AIBP/Bharat
Nirman to Andhra Pradesh
*669. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh has requested the Central
Government for enhancement of allocation
of funds under AIBP/Bharat Nirman during
the next five years and also to revise the
norm for making allocation and extending
loans under AIBP;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) the status of the above request and
by when this request is likely to be
accepted; and

request of Andhra Pradesh?
Gas from Myanmar

SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Myanmar has refused to
export gas to India from its offshore block
A-1 and potential reserves in block A-3;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether ONGC (Videsh) and GAIL
have 30 per cent stake in these blocks; and
(d) the impact of this decision on
GAIL's proposal for a pipeline from
Myanmar through North-Eastern States to
West Bengal and Bihar to transport gas from
A-1 and A-3?

Jagannath Temple in Puri
*671. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government
propose to renovate some of the 400 odd
muths around the Jagannath Temple in
Puri, Orissa to boost religious tourism;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Central Government
propose to fund the project; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

Congestion in Delhi and Mumbai
airports
*672. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are taking any
steps to address the problem of congestion
in Delhi and Mumbai airports while the
expansion projects are on;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Rapid exit taxiway at Chennai
airport
*673. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal for
construction of rapid exit taxiway at
Chennai airport;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, whether any similar type of
facilities have been extended to other
airports in the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Joint venture between British Gas
and ONGC
*674. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the joint
venture between the British Gas and
ONGC for developing the 3 KG Basin
blocks has been dropped by Government;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether arbitrary denial for JV will
lower the image of Government among
global investors; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken to restore
the JV between British Gas and ONGC
which has been conducted through a
transparent bidding process?
Allotment of petrol pumps
*675. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of petrol pumps as
on 31st March, 2007;
(b) the details for both public and
private companies, company-wise; and
(c) the number of petrol pumps, which
were given to ex-servicemen, freedom
fighters and other VIPs during the period
2004 to 31st March, 2007?
Loans in domestic priority sector for
minorities
†*676. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been an increase
of 33 per cent in the amount of loan in
domestic priority sector for the minorities
upto March 31, 2007;
(b) whether it is a fact that the amount
of loan for the minorities is contemplated
to be increased further; and
(c) whether various programmes and
proper schemes will also be formulated for
the minorities apart from increasing the
amount of loan?

Extra charges by banks on credit
card  holders
*677. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
credit card holders in India pay the highest
rates of interest in the world and have been
ripped of Rs. 6,000 crore as extra charges
by banks in a span of ten years;
(b) if so, whether these charges are
collected in the name of late fee, cash
advance fee, billed finance fee, over-limit
fee, cash withdrawal fee, cheque pick up
fee and service taxes etc.;
(c) whether these charges levied by these
private banks are consistent with RBI
regulations; and
(d) if not, what action Government
propose to take in this regard?
Completion of river linking project
*678. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) what is the time-frame decided for
the completion of river linking project;
(b) whether Government have taken a
view over the action plans one and two of
the river linking project;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) if not, the reasons for the delay; and
(e) whether Government expects to be
able to adhere to the time-frame?
Inclination towards capitalism in the
country
†*679. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the recent statement by the
Prime Minister during inauguration
function of Institute for Studies in
Industrial Development wherein he has
expressed his apprehension regarding
inclination to capitalism in the country;
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto;
(c) whether it is being proposed to
change the economic policy of the country
in view of the above statement; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Misuse of tax exemptions
*680. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
too many tax exemptions, paraded as
incentives, make tax administration
vulnerable to misuse;
(b) what were the total tax exemptions/
concessions granted during the year, 2004-
05 as compared to the year, 2005-06; and
(c) what steps Government propose to
take for making any foolproof system, so
that the misuse can be restricted during the
current year?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 16th May, 2007 Secretary-General.
